title: The induced grading of a homogeneous coordinate quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $N\ge0$, and give $B=k[z_0,\ldots,z_N]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] its total-degree standard grading [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $J$ be a homogeneous ideal of $B$. In the actual quotient ring $A=B/J$, define $A_m$ to be the image of the degree-$m$ polynomial submodule under the quotient map $q:B\to A$. These specified submodules have a unique nonnegative graded-algebra decomposition, with the degree-$m$ projection satisfying $\pi_m(q(b))=q(\pi_m(b))$ for every polynomial $b$. The induced grading is this unique decomposition of these explicit images. This includes $J=B$ and the zero quotient.
